cards.front: A stem cell {{c1::self-renews}} when its stem-cell pool persists over long periods.
cards.quote: self-renews, meaning that a stem-cell pool persists over long periods
cards.section: What the lineage trace proves—and what it does not

cards.front: What two functional properties define a stem-cell population?
cards.back: It produces differentiated descendants and maintains its own stem-cell pool over long periods.
cards.quote: A stem-cell population produces differentiated descendants and self-renews, meaning that a stem-cell pool persists over long periods.
cards.section: What the lineage trace proves—and what it does not

cards.front: Why does observing one cell division not establish self-renewal?
cards.back: Transit-amplifying cells also divide briefly before differentiating. Self-renewal requires sustained maintenance of the stem-cell pool.
cards.quote: One division proves little because transit-amplifying cells, short-lived progenitors that divide a few times and then differentiate, also copy themselves briefly.
cards.section: What the lineage trace proves—and what it does not

cards.front: A cultured cell divides several times. What stronger result would test whether it self-renews?
cards.back: Show repeated growth and replating from that one cell. Sustained propagation tests persistence rather than brief proliferation.
cards.quote: Repeated growth and replating from one cultured cell or transplantation through successive hosts can test persistence.
cards.section: What the lineage trace proves—and what it does not

cards.front: Short-lived progenitors that divide a few times and then differentiate are {{c1::transit-amplifying cells}}.
cards.quote: transit-amplifying cells, short-lived progenitors that divide a few times and then differentiate
cards.section: What the lineage trace proves—and what it does not

cards.front: Lgr5 is expressed in cycling crypt-base cells. Why is a long-term lineage trace still needed to identify stem cells?
cards.back: Expression only marks cells at one time. Inherited labels reveal whether their descendants show sustained, multilineage output—the functional stem-cell test.
cards.quote: Expression is a marker, not a fate test.
cards.section: What the lineage trace proves—and what it does not

cards.front: What does a 60-day Lgr5 lineage trace that fills ribbons containing every intestinal epithelial lineage support?
cards.back: The initially labelled population contains stem cells with sustained, multilineage output.
cards.quote: That sustained, multilineage output supports the conclusion that the labelled population contains stem cells
cards.section: What the lineage trace proves—and what it does not

cards.front: Why does production of every intestinal epithelial lineage demonstrate multipotency rather than pluripotency?
cards.back: Those are several cell types within one tissue. Pluripotency requires the ability to make all lineages of the embryo proper.
cards.quote: It shows multipotency, production of several cell types within one tissue, not pluripotency
cards.section: What the lineage trace proves—and what it does not

cards.front: A long-term trace contains labelled cells from every intestinal epithelial lineage, but some initial clones disappeared. Does clone loss refute the stem-cell conclusion, and why?
cards.back: No. The population shows sustained, multilineage output; the result does not require every initially marked cell to survive.
cards.quote: it does not mean every initially marked cell survives.
cards.section: What the lineage trace proves—and what it does not

cards.front: A renewing tissue contains cycling stem cells whose divisions are often symmetric. Does this violate the functional definition of a stem cell? Explain.
cards.back: No. The definition rests on differentiated output and long-term pool maintenance, not dormancy or one asymmetric outcome from every division.
cards.quote: Stem cells need not be dormant, and their definition does not require one stem and one differentiated daughter from every division.
cards.section: What the lineage trace proves—and what it does not

cards.front: Chance competition among equivalent lineages for limited stem-cell positions is {{c1::neutral drift}}.
cards.quote: That pattern is neutral drift, chance competition among equivalent lineages for limited stem-cell positions.
cards.section: Put neutral drift to work

cards.front: What clone pattern supports neutral drift among intestinal stem cells?
cards.back: Over time, surviving clones grow while other clones vanish as equivalent lineages compete for limited positions.
cards.quote: over 1 to 6 months surviving clones grew while others vanished.
cards.section: Put neutral drift to work

cards.front: One marked stem cell starts in each of 100 crypts. If each crypt has five equivalent competitors, how many crypts are expected to become fully labelled?
cards.back: Win probability = 1/5. Expected labelled crypts = 100 × 1/5 = 20; the other 80 marked clones are lost.
cards.quote: Suppose each crypt has an effective pool of five equivalent competitors
cards.section: Put neutral drift to work

cards.front: A population began with 100 marked stem cells. At an intermediate time, 50 marked clones survive. What is their mean size?
cards.back: Mean size = 100 marked cells ÷ 50 surviving clones = 2 cells per surviving clone.
cards.quote: At an intermediate time with 50 surviving clones, their mean size is 100/50 = 2 cells
cards.section: Put neutral drift to work

cards.front: In 100 crypts with five competitors each, one marked cell starts per crypt. How can 20 fully labelled crypts at the end preserve the marked population on average?
cards.back: The start has 100 × 1 = 100 marked cells; the expected end has 20 × 5 = 100. Clone loss is balanced by survivor expansion.
cards.why: Neutral drift balances the population in expectation, not in each individual crypt.
cards.quote: The point of the arithmetic is population balance on average.
cards.section: Put neutral drift to work

cards.front: If every stem-cell division instead produced exactly one stem cell and one transit-amplifying cell, what would happen to clone size?
cards.back: Each clone would retain one stem cell rather than randomly expanding or vanishing; pool size would be fixed by asymmetric division.
cards.quote: If every division produced one stem cell and one transit-amplifying cell, pool size would be fixed by asymmetric division.
cards.section: Put neutral drift to work

cards.front: Why can the effective number of competing crypt stem cells differ from the number counted?
cards.back: Positions have unequal short-term survival odds, and cell movement between positions makes the long-term outcome appear neutral.
cards.quote: cells at the crypt bottom survive better than cells at its edge, but movement between positions makes the months-long outcome look neutral.
cards.section: The fuller neutral-drift picture

cards.front: The local environment whose contact and signals bias stem-cell retention versus differentiation is the {{c1::stem-cell niche}}.
cards.quote: A stem-cell niche is the local environment whose contact and signals bias whether a daughter retains a stem-cell position or differentiates.
cards.section: The niche: what limits a stem-cell position

cards.front: At the crypt base, {{c1::Wnt signalling}} is strongest and promotes self-renewal.
cards.quote: Wnt signalling is strongest at the crypt base and promotes self-renewal
cards.section: The niche: what limits a stem-cell position

cards.front: Higher among differentiated cells, {{c1::BMP}} is strongest and suppresses self-renewal.
cards.quote: BMP is strongest higher among differentiated cells and suppresses self-renewal.
cards.section: The niche: what limits a stem-cell position

cards.front: Why are daughters moving upward from the crypt base more likely to differentiate?
cards.back: They move away from base signals that support self-renewal and toward stronger BMP, which suppresses self-renewal.
cards.quote: As daughters move up, they become more likely to leave the stem state.
cards.section: The niche: what limits a stem-cell position

cards.front: Adding a source of support tests {{c1::sufficiency}}, whereas removing it in the animal tests requirement.
cards.quote: adding support tests sufficiency, whereas removing it in the animal tests requirement.
cards.section: The niche: what limits a stem-cell position

cards.front: Single sorted Lgr5 cells form organoids and can be replated repeatedly without stromal cells. What does this establish, and what caveat remains?
cards.back: It establishes sustained growth from single cells under those conditions. Matrigel and added factors still provide a niche, so the cells were not unsupported.
cards.quote: No stromal cells were present, although matrix and added factors still supplied a niche
cards.section: The niche: what limits a stem-cell position

cards.front: Paneth-cell co-culture improves organoid formation, and a Wnt pulse can replace Paneth cells. What does this show and not show?
cards.back: Paneth cells can provide support in that culture: sufficiency. It does not show that living gut stem cells require Paneth cells because another source may substitute.
cards.quote: Paneth cells can supply support under those culture conditions: a sufficiency result.
cards.section: The niche: what limits a stem-cell position

cards.front: Removing one proposed niche source causes no renewal defect. Can the source be declared unnecessary? Explain.
cards.back: Not necessarily. Another source may have compensated. Requirement is better supported by loss, and loss followed by rescue is especially strong.
cards.quote: Loss followed by rescue is especially strong; no failure after removal can mean that another source compensated.
cards.section: The niche: what limits a stem-cell position

cards.front: Design an in vivo test of whether Paneth cells are indispensable for intestinal stem-cell maintenance.
cards.back: Ablate Paneth cells selectively, confirm their removal, then measure Lgr5-positive cells, EdU incorporation, and output from a separate Lgr5 lineage-tracing pulse over days to weeks.
cards.quote: Express the human diphtheria-toxin receptor from a Paneth-cell lysozyme gene, then give toxin to ablate Paneth cells while sparing other cells.
cards.section: Design problem

cards.front: In a selective Paneth-cell ablation, what outcomes distinguish a Paneth-only niche from substitutable support?
cards.back: Paneth-only support predicts loss of Lgr5 cells and stalled renewal. Substitutable support predicts that stem cells may persist after ablation.
cards.quote: If Paneth cells are the only niche, their ablation should remove Lgr5 cells and stall renewal
cards.section: Design problem

cards.front: Deleting Porcn in FOXL1-positive telocytes rapidly reduces crypt Wnt signalling and proliferation. What does this result show?
cards.back: Wnt secretion from those telocytes is required for normal crypt Wnt signalling and proliferation under those conditions.
cards.quote: telocyte Porcn deletion reduced crypt Wnt signalling and proliferation within 24 hours in 2018
cards.section: Design problem

cards.front: What controls make a diphtheria-toxin Paneth-cell ablation test interpretable?
cards.back: Use toxin-treated mice lacking the receptor, receptor mice without toxin, and staining that confirms Paneth-cell removal.
cards.quote: Controls include toxin in mice without the receptor, receptor mice without toxin, staining to confirm Paneth-cell removal
cards.section: Design problem

cards.front: When a progenitor regains a tissue stem-cell state, it has {{c1::dedifferentiated}}.
cards.quote: dedifferentiated, meaning that they regained a tissue stem-cell state.
cards.section: After injury, other cells can refill the stem pool

cards.front: Secretory precursors are labelled before Lgr5-positive cells are killed. Later, labelled Lgr5-positive cells and epithelial ribbons appear. What is the narrowest conclusion?
cards.back: The labelled precursors regained a stem-cell state after injury and produced descendants that rebuilt the epithelium.
cards.quote: Labelled precursors regained a stem-cell state after injury
cards.section: After injury, other cells can refill the stem pool

cards.front: Why does injury-induced stem-cell activity in gut progenitors not contradict their usual role in normal renewal?
cards.back: The regained activity occurs after injury, a distinct condition; it does not show that those progenitors are normal stem cells before injury.
cards.quote: This is a distinct condition, not an exception to the film's homeostatic result.
cards.section: After injury, other cells can refill the stem pool

cards.front: What did the timing and requirement of ASCL2 show during gut repair after lethal Lgr5-cell injury?
cards.back: Progenitors switched on Ascl2 before Lgr5, and restoration required ASCL2, linking ASCL2 to recovery of stem-cell activity.
cards.quote: They switched on Ascl2 days before Lgr5, and restoration required ASCL2.
cards.section: After injury, other cells can refill the stem pool

cards.front: A gut progenitor regains stem-cell activity after injury. Why is this not evidence of pluripotency?
cards.back: It regained a tissue stem-cell state and rebuilt gut epithelium. Pluripotency requires production of the embryo proper's lineages, beyond one tissue.
cards.quote: Regaining gut stem activity is not becoming pluripotent
cards.section: After injury, other cells can refill the stem pool

cards.front: A cell able to make one cell type is {{c1::unipotent}}.
cards.quote: A unipotent cell makes one type
cards.section: Resetting beyond one tissue: Gurdon to Yamanaka

cards.front: A cell able to make several cell types within one tissue is {{c1::multipotent}}.
cards.quote: a multipotent cell makes several types within one tissue
cards.section: Resetting beyond one tissue: Gurdon to Yamanaka

cards.front: A cell able to make the embryo proper's lineages is {{c1::pluripotent}}.
cards.quote: a pluripotent cell makes the embryo proper's lineages
cards.section: Resetting beyond one tissue: Gurdon to Yamanaka

cards.front: A cell able to make an entire conceptus, including extra-embryonic tissues, is {{c1::totipotent}}.
cards.quote: a totipotent cell can make an entire conceptus, including placenta and other extra-embryonic tissues.
cards.section: Resetting beyond one tissue: Gurdon to Yamanaka

cards.front: What did normal tadpoles produced by transplanting intestinal-cell nuclei into eggs whose own nuclei had been destroyed demonstrate?
cards.back: At least some specialized nuclei retained the instructions needed for development, and egg cytoplasm could read those instructions.
cards.quote: Each normal tadpole directed by a transplanted nucleus shows that at least that specialized nucleus retained the needed instructions
cards.section: Resetting beyond one tissue: Gurdon to Yamanaka

cards.front: Most nuclear-transfer eggs fail, but a few become normal tadpoles under control of the transplanted intestinal nucleus. Do the failures show that specialized nuclei discard developmental genes?
cards.back: No. Each success shows that its specialized nucleus retained the needed instructions. Failures alone cannot identify what was missing.
cards.quote: Failures alone cannot identify what was missing, and a genetic nuclear marker ruled out a surviving egg nucleus.
cards.section: Resetting beyond one tissue: Gurdon to Yamanaka

cards.front: How were mouse fibroblasts first reset to induced pluripotent stem cells in the lesson's example?
cards.back: Four transcription factors—Oct3/4, Sox2, Klf4 and c-Myc—were used under embryonic-stem-cell culture conditions.
cards.quote: used four transcription factors—Oct3/4, Sox2, Klf4 and c-Myc—to turn mouse fibroblasts into induced pluripotent stem (iPS) cells
cards.section: Resetting beyond one tissue: Gurdon to Yamanaka

cards.front: Mouse iPS cells contribute to tissues from all three embryonic germ layers. Which potency claim does this support, and which stronger claim remains untested?
cards.back: It supports pluripotency. It does not establish totipotency because it does not show that one cell can form an entire conceptus with extra-embryonic tissues.
cards.quote: The result spans the embryo proper's lineages.
cards.section: Resetting beyond one tissue: Gurdon to Yamanaka

cards.front: What common conclusion follows from successful nuclear transfer and induction of pluripotency, and what conclusion does neither establish?
cards.back: At least some specialized nuclei retain developmental instructions that can be reset. Neither result shows that the specialized cell itself became totipotent.
cards.quote: Neither result shows that a specialized cell itself became totipotent
cards.section: Resetting beyond one tissue: Gurdon to Yamanaka

cards.front: How did chromosome-marked spleen colonies establish a functional stem-cell assay pattern?
cards.back: Each colony was shown to be a clone, and later colonies contained new colony-forming cells, providing evidence of self-renewal.
cards.quote: chromosome markers showed that each colony was a clone.
cards.section: The functional definition came before Lgr5

cards.front: Why are untreated mice necessary controls in CreERT2 lineage tracing?
cards.back: Some Cre can enter the nucleus without tamoxifen, so untreated animals reveal background recombination caused by leakiness.
cards.quote: Some Cre can leak into the nucleus without tamoxifen, so untreated mice are a necessary control.
cards.section: How Cre lineage tracing works

cards.front: If each crypt has 14 effective competitors and one clone is initially marked in each of 100 crypts, about how many fully labelled crypts are expected?
cards.back: Expected winners = 100 × 1/14 = 7.14, so about 7 fully labelled crypts.
cards.quote: With N = 14, 100 starting clones give 100/14, about 7, fully labelled crypts in expectation
cards.section: The fuller neutral-drift picture

cards.front: Why does producing one induced pluripotent stem-cell line not prove that every such line is equivalent to an embryonic stem-cell line?
cards.back: Reprogramming can produce pluripotency, but the result does not show that every iPS line matches embryonic stem cells in every test.
cards.quote: Reprogramming does not show that every iPS line matches embryonic stem cells in every test.
cards.section: Early and later iPS lines
